summary: This paper presents a branch-resolved characterization framework for feed-forward error in dynamic quantum teleportation on superconducting processors, reconstructing branch Choi operators via classical shadows and comparing three correction strategies across two physical qubit layouts. Experiments on IBM Fez with perfect and symmetric W$_4$ resource states reveal a reversal in the relative effectiveness of post-processing versus PROM mitigation depending on mid-circuit measurement readout error, with feed-forward penalties ranging from 0.02–0.03 (low readout error layout) to ~0.07 (high readout error layout).
motivation: Mid-circuit measurement and classical feed-forward are essential for dynamic circuits, but their errors remain poorly characterized at the branch level; existing outcome-aggregated analyses fail to expose branch-specific error structure and discrepancies between mitigation strategies.
method: The authors designed controlled W$_4$ state preparations (maximally entangled perfect W$_4$ and non-maximally entangled symmetric W$_4$) with matched depths and gate counts, reconstructed branch Choi operators on a reference-output qubit pair using classical Choi shadows, and compared physical correction, post-processing, and BFA-based PROM mitigation across two layouts chosen to have high (qubits 6, 5) and low (qubits 23, 16) readout assignment error.
result: Layout 1 (higher RAE ~0.05) showed aggregate feed-forward penalty $\Delta_{\mathrm{FF}} \approx 0.02$–0.03 with PROM mean gain $\bar{G}_q \approx 0.03$–0.05; layout 2 (lower RAE ~0.006) showed $\Delta_{\mathrm{FF}} \approx 0.07$ with $\bar{G}_q \approx 0.01$–0.02, demonstrating that readout noise level inverts the relative ranking of post-processing and PROM effectiveness across all measurement branches.
